name: Ranibizumab
route_note: intravitreal injection monthly or less often; refillable ocular implant (Susvimo) every six months
owner: Genentech/Roche (US); Novartis (outside US); biosimilars (Samsung Bioepis/Biogen, Sandoz and others)

discovery.note: An affinity-matured humanised Fab fragment derived from the same mouse anti-VEGF antibody as bevacizumab, designed for intraocular use. Year the affinity-matured anti-VEGF Fab was first described (Chen et al., J. Mol. Biol. 1999).

tagline: Anti-VEGF antibody fragment that turned wet macular degeneration into a treatable disease
summary: Ranibizumab is a humanised antibody fragment that binds all isoforms of VEGF-A. Injected into the eye, it suppresses abnormal blood vessel growth and leakage in neovascular age-related macular degeneration and other retinal diseases, and was the first treatment to improve vision on average in wet AMD.
mechanism: Vascular endothelial growth factor A drives choroidal and retinal neovascularisation and increases vascular permeability, causing leakage, oedema and haemorrhage in the macula.

Ranibizumab binds the receptor-binding site of active VEGF-A isoforms, preventing VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 activation. Lacking an Fc region, it is small enough to penetrate the retina and is cleared quickly from the circulation.
uses: Diabetic macular oedema and diabetic retinopathy
Macular oedema after retinal vein occlusion

history.title: VEGF cloned
history.detail: Napoleone Ferrara's group at Genentech isolates and clones VEGF.

history.title: MARINA and ANCHOR
history.detail: Monthly ranibizumab improves vision in wet AMD; FDA approves Lucentis.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: Authorised in the EU, marketed by Novartis.

history.title: CATT trial
history.detail: Bevacizumab is shown to be similarly effective at much lower cost, fuelling debate about off-label use.

history.title: First ophthalmic biosimilar
history.detail: FDA approves Byooviz and the Susvimo port delivery system.

history.title: Susvimo recall
history.detail: Genentech recalls the Susvimo implant over septum dislodgement; it returns to market in 2024.

pk.half_life: about 9 days in the vitreous; about 2 hours systemic

safety.boxed_warning: Susvimo implant: endophthalmitis has occurred at three times the rate of monthly intravitreal ranibizumab.

facts: Ranibizumab is a Fab fragment of about 48 kDa with no Fc region, unlike the full-length antibody bevacizumab made from the same parent mouse antibody.
Byooviz (ranibizumab-nuna), approved by the FDA in September 2021, was the first biosimilar approved in the US to treat eye disease.
Susvimo, a refillable ocular implant that delivers ranibizumab continuously, was approved in the US in October 2021.

references.title: Chen Y et al. Selection and analysis of an optimized anti-VEGF antibody (J Mol Biol 1999)
FDA: FDA approves first biosimilar to treat macular degeneration disease and other eye conditions (2021)
